checks.name: Copied source rows match their preserved checksums
Native PostgreSQL contains 20 Material identities and 48 real source tasks
The original 30-site display cell and 15-site calculation cell coexist correctly
Both legacy final-structure formats are adapted
Unreported pressure stays null; no thermodynamic energy is invented
Existing source Phase exposes real pressure points 1, 15 and 60 GPa
Reimport reuses the same receipt, Material IDs and Calculation IDs
Concurrent first imports allocate each Material only once
Nine real static calculations can be added later without changing Material IDs
A second source with the same known-pressure display geometry reuses Material
Conflicting source task content is rejected atomically
Wrong-composition output does not leave a partial calculation
PostgreSQL rejects another Material’s property selection
PostgreSQL rejects a calculation-cell atom-count mismatch
Stored geometry and Material pressure cannot be overwritten
PostgreSQL → transfer package → SQLite preserves every logical row and ID
PostgreSQL and SQLite return identical Material detail contracts
SQLite also enforces property ownership and geometry immutability
SQLite → transfer package → fresh PostgreSQL preserves the same dataset
MongoDB document conversion is lossless (no MongoDB server tested)
Recomputed package checksum cannot hide mismatched structure metadata
HTTP API reads native PostgreSQL records and serves the inspection page

runtime.version: PostgreSQL 18.4 on x86_64-apple-darwin24.6.0, compiled by Apple clang version 17.0.0 (clang-1700.6.3.2), 64-bit

limits: 20 selected source materials, not a production-scale benchmark.
Physical equivalence matching beyond exact display representation is not implemented.
Source E definitions/method compatibility are unverified; no scientific enthalpy or hull result was generated.
MongoDB document conversion was tested without a MongoDB server.
